debate_title: Compute governance as a lever for AI safety: export contr...

conflicts.point: Whether federal agencies can legally and effectively enforce mandatory telemetry, runtime inspections, and trade-secret overrides on advanced AI systems.

positions.stance: Agencies can adapt statutory oversight mechanisms through conditional operating licenses and runtime telemetry, mirroring aviation and financial sector regulations.
Statutory inspection rights and compliance mandates are technically and legally unworkable given distributed cloud architectures and continuous parameter updates.
Horizontal agencies lack the statutory authority and technical workforce to enforce such inspections, turning compliance frameworks into corporate capture tools.

verdicts.conflict: Whether federal agencies can legally and effectively enforce mandatory telemetry, runtime inspections, and trade-secret overrides on advanced AI systems.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist critique successfully highlights the functional difference between static physical assets like aircraft and dynamic software systems that undergo continuous iteration. Safetyist analogies to aviation and banking fail to account for the continuous post-deployment fine-tuning characteristic of neural network weights.
